title: OER or Not Classifier
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: Place eleven resource cards in three bins (Open OER, Free but not open, Not free and not open) to see that openness comes from the license, not the price.

learningObjectives: The learner will classify each of 11 described resources as open (OER), free but not open, or not free and not open, by checking its license and public-domain status rather than its price.
prerequisites: The terms educational resource, copyright, license, public domain, open license, free resource, and open educational resource

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, commit an answer, and read the reason
keyQuestions: Does a license or the public domain grant permission?
Does the price change whether a resource is open?
commonMisconceptions: A resource that is free to download is OER
A resource must be free of charge to be open
A resource posted publicly with no license statement may be reused
assessmentOpportunities: A quiz bank under CC0 is sold on a marketplace for $5. Which bin?
A video streams free of charge and shows no license. Which bin?
Why is a photograph taken by a NASA employee as part of their job an open resource?
What single question separates the Open bin from the other two?

controls.name: Three bin buttons
controls.description: place the current card. The placement is final.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves to the next card after you read the feedback.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: on a narrow screen the bin definitions move behind this button.

controls.name: Previous missed / Next missed
controls.description: on the results screen, page through the cards you missed.

controls.name: Play again
controls.description: shuffles the cards for a practice run.
